page: Vultr vx1-g-48c-192g is a dedicated general-purpose instance within the VX1 Cloud Compute family. Powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC processor running at 2.0 GHz, the server provides 48 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 24 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading. It features 192 GB of system RAM, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4 GB per virtual core. Cache structures include 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. Advanced CPU instruction support includes AVX-512 extensions (f, vnni, bf16) alongside cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA-NI.

Benchmark evaluations position this instance in the top tier for single-core and multi-core processing, achieving 2607.0 in Geekbench single-core and 22510.0 in multi-core metrics. Uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 428.71 GB/sec, while write operations achieve 201.63 GB/sec, placing memory throughput in the top decile. In specialized workloads, it delivers high performance in static web serving at 85.98 GB/sec and in-memory key-value operations with 91.43 million Redis SET operations per second. CPU-based machine learning inference is also notable, generating 69.0 tokens per second on 7B parameter models and 7.3 tokens per second on 70B models.

A clear operational tradeoff is local storage capacity. While the system provisions a fast NVMe SSD, it is allocated at only 1 GB, and the instance includes no hardware GPUs. Data persistence, persistent database logging, and large application binaries therefore depend heavily on networked block storage. The density of 48 dedicated cores combined with high memory bandwidth delivers strong compute efficiency for memory-heavy and compute-intensive operations without requiring hyper-scale GPU infrastructure. Workloads best aligned with this configuration include parallel code compilation, in-memory databases, continuous integration pipelines, static content delivery, and enterprise application hosting.
